scope: Public source-specific authoring companion. It supplies runnable config grammar, not a scientific grid choice, execution authorization, runtime validation or FES convergence. Preserve the original workflow and pinned input; current user delegation governs Prepare/Execute while required artifact/runtime checks remain separate.

applicability.source_match: Exact registered raw hashes only; EOL-normalized equality to the declared committed public revision was separately checked. Source mismatch/unavailability means reference_only, not current effective defaults.
applicability.remote_freshness: not independently established; no current remote HEAD claim
applicability.selected_executable_support: not_run; source registration is not executable/source correspondence

studio_binding.guidance: Use describe_engine and existing authoring context. Bind the authorized same-producer OPES_COLVAR and save fes.yaml in the current owned input root. Save/readback and actual hashes are authoring evidence only; no shell, grant change, automatic submission or numerical data reconstructed from chat.

log_input.format: UTF8 #! FIELDS name... before numeric rows; optional #! SET key value metadata; repeated field headers must agree; numeric rows must match field count; all values finite. Headerless GASCV rejected.
log_input.identity: Read actual run.id plus collected results-relative artifact name. A run directory basename is not a run ID. read_artifact supports extensionless text; read_project_input may return metadata-only for OPES_COLVAR. Do not rename or fabricate data to bypass classification.
log_input.scope: Sample rows and columns must come from the pinned real log. The example below is illustrative, never the answer for a real case.

fes_yaml.serialization: YAML mapping; these are the only keys consumed by _run_opes_reweight. A field name in a planning note is not a saved config.

cv_columns.type: nonempty list of exact header names
cv_columns.guidance: Read actual #! FIELDS. Preserve the requested CVs; no atom groups or CV meaning are inferred from a column label.

temperature.guidance: Reuse the actual sampling temperature and its provenance. No implicit scientific default.

bins.guidance: One per selected CV; a one-element list broadcasts for multiple CVs. Preserve the user grid; no convergence claim from fine bins.

lower.guidance: Each lower < matching upper. Bounds are scientific choices, not software defaults.

periodic.guidance: True wraps each value into [lower,upper). Use established CV periodicity; omission is a code default, not evidence of nonperiodicity.

extra_bias_columns.guidance: Explicitly select the logged extra_bias when it is the separately applied contribution required for native total-bias weights. Merely having an extra_bias column does not activate it. Avoid double-counting a contribution already included in the selected bias column.

blocks.guidance: For blocks>1, produce blocks-1 prefix-to-full RMSE values. blocks<=1 produces no prefix comparisons. This is not independent block standard error.

fes_yaml.unsupported_override: logweight_column is NOT read by this CLI. It recomputes weights from selected bias columns. Extra YAML keys are not validated by this function and may be silently ignored; do not invent controls.
fes_yaml.example_purpose: Syntactically valid one-CV illustration for a log with cv_0, bias and extra_bias. Temperature300, range[-1,1], bins32 and blocks2 are examples, not inferred defaults or production choices. Replace using established task inputs; ask only unresolved scientific choices.
fes_yaml.example_yaml:
cv_columns: [cv_0]
temperature: 300
bins: [32]
lower: [-1.0]
upper: [1.0]
periodic: [false]
bias_column: bias
extra_bias_columns: [extra_bias]
blocks: 2

weights.formula: V_total = selected bias_column + sum(selected extra_bias_columns); beta = 1/(8.617333262145e-5 eV/K * temperature); log_weights = beta*V_total - max(beta*V_total); w=exp(log_weights).
weights.native_equivalence: For native OPES logs with matching producer kBT and eV/K units, select bias and extra_bias to reproduce (bias + extra_bias)/kBT up to a constant shift, matching base/opes.py opes_logweight. That logweight column is a diagnostic cross-check, not a CLI override.
weights.not_wtmetad: Do NOT subtract rct/c(t) or zed. Those are OPES diagnostics, not WTMetaD offsets. Do not apply WT bias-factor scaling.
weights.ess: ESS=(sum(w)^2)/sum(w^2), over all input rows before range exclusion; it does not establish independent samples or physical convergence.

grid_and_support.dimension: Complete CLI export supports one or two selected CVs because default PNG rendering rejects higher dimensions. Numerical histogram capability alone does not establish a complete higher-dimensional CLI route.
grid_and_support.histogram: Weighted histogram over supplied ranges, normalized to in-range mass. Nonperiodic out-of-range samples do not contribute; zero histogram mass raises. Periodic samples wrap before histogramming. Axes are bin centers.
grid_and_support.empty_bins: Probability0 stays F=+inf; occupied bins use -kBT*log(probability) and minimum occupied F shifted to0. Do not replace empty bins by finite values or infer unsampled barriers.
grid_and_support.reported_support: Report samples, finite_bins/total_bins, ESS and grid. Sparse short data is an engineering check, not converged FES or a barrier estimate.
grid_and_support.units: FES, selected bias/extra bias and block RMSE are eV; temperature K; CV axes retain declared CV units.

blocks_semantics.algorithm: For b in range(1,blocks), stop=max(1,N*b//blocks). Recompute histogram from samples[:stop],weights[:stop], compare to full FES on finite-overlap bins after each surface own zero shift. RMSE=sqrt(mean((prefix-full)^2)).
blocks_semantics.blocks2: One comparison: first floor(N/2) samples (at least1) versus full trajectory. It is not a split into independent halves and not standard error.
blocks_semantics.limits: Overlapping prefixes are correlated; finite-overlap may omit unsupported bins; no overlap yields NaN. A zero RMSE does not prove convergence.

outputs.OPES_FES.txt: Flattened meshgrid(indexing=ij) rows: selected CV center columns, probability, free_energy_eV. Last CV index changes fastest. Empty bins remain inf.
outputs.OPES_FES.npz: axes, probability, free_energy, normalized log_weights, effective_sample_size, block_rmse. Serialized output is not a new input/source proof.
outputs.OPES_FES.png: One-CV line or two-CV contour; no physical convergence claim.
outputs.OPES_FES_summary.json: effective_sample_size, samples, finite_bins, total_bins, block_rmse_eV, weighting=exp(beta * total_instantaneous_bias), rct_used=false.
outputs.defaults: These output basenames are CLI defaults and are used by the Studio adapter. Direct CLI flags --fes-out/--npz-out/--png-out/--summary-out may change them; no default device/GPU flag for opes-reweight.
